sign-a-bundle-of-unsigned-transactions-f.text: Issue 639, second of five tickets under issue 490. This page records the story, the bundle format, the requirements and the refusals. Submitting witnesses (issue 640) and the write commands that write bundles (issue 641) are not part of it.

story.text: As Bob, I receive a bundle of unsigned transactions and run singular wallet sign --vault bob.vault bundle.json on an offline machine. I type my passphrase and get one witness file per transaction next to the bundle, with a short summary of what I signed on standard error. My key never leaves the vault and the command opens no network connection.

the-bundle.text: One JSON file with a version field, currently 1. It holds the name of the command that wrote it, the network magic, the registry state token (null before a registry exists), the addresses that must sign, and the transactions in submission order. Each transaction holds its identity, its unsigned body as a standard text envelope (Unwitnessed Tx ConwayEra), its deadline (the body's validity upper bound, or null) and the effects its writer expects as plain-language lines. The effects are the writer's claims: they are shown and journaled, never trusted.

requirements.text: bundle-round-trips: decoding what encoding wrote gives the same bundle, transactions in order, for more than one transaction.

limits-recorded.text: Whether the signers list is complete cannot be checked offline, because inputs cannot be resolved; submit checks the witness set against the chain. Expiry is not judged offline, because there is no clock that knows the slot; submit refuses expired bodies.
